newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Kelon mulls expansion in share capital.
newsitem.headline: Kelon mulls expansion in share capital.

text.p: Chinese refrigerator maker Guangdong Kelon Electrical Holdings Co Ltd said it was considering expanding share capital as one way of raising capital to fund its production expansion plan.

"We hope, in an upcoming general meeting, to seek shareholders' approval to empower the board of directors the fexibility to place shares," said Don Lee, vice president of Kelon, in an earnings presentation on Friday.
"However, it is at a very preliminary stage," Lee said. "We have to consult with lawyers and have to get Chinese authority approval before it can come to reality."
H-share companies, the mainland Chinese enterprises listed in Hong Kong, have to get the Chinese regulatory authority's approval for any new share issues.

Due to rapid development of the company's strategies for developing a nationwide production network and its plan for acquiring component manufacturing capabilities, Kelon said it was considering alternatives to finace such growth including the possibility of raising capital through an equity issue.

"In view of our existing plans for 1997, we have sufficient cash on hand to fund the projects and we do not have any urgent need to raise fund," Lee said. Kelon has about 650 million yuan cash on hand as at the end of 1996, he said.
Kelon reported a 55.2 percent rise in net profit to 439.8 million yuan for year ended December 31, 1996.
